title: A Spray-On Powder That Stops Bleeding in Seconds
hook: A new spray-on powder can stop life-threatening bleeding in about one second by instantly forming a gel over the wound — even on deep, irregular injuries.
key_points: Developed by KAIST, the powder forms a strong gel over a wound almost instantly when sprayed on.
It works on deep, irregular wounds where standard hemostatic products often struggle.
It reportedly stays effective even after years of storage in harsh conditions.
Originally designed for battlefield use, it could also improve care in ambulances, ERs, and disasters.
content_html: Stopping severe bleeding fast is one of the most important things a bystander or medic can do — and a new material developed by KAIST researchers, covered by ScienceDaily, promises to make that dramatically faster. The spray-on powder forms a strong gel over a wound in about one second, working even on deep and irregular injuries where conventional hemostatic products often struggle.
extra_html: Two details make this more than a lab curiosity: the powder reportedly stays effective even after years of storage in harsh conditions, and it was originally engineered for battlefield trauma, one of the toughest environments for keeping medical supplies reliable. If it holds up outside the lab, the same qualities that make it useful for combat medics could translate to ambulances, disaster response, and hospital emergency rooms — anywhere fast, dependable bleeding control matters most. It's still a research development, not yet a product on pharmacy shelves; the basics of direct pressure remain what to do right now for severe bleeding.

related.title: Stopping Severe Bleeding
related.hook: Severe bleeding can become life-threatening in minutes. Firm, direct pressure is the single most important thing a bystander can do — and you do it now, not later.
